%   the first-order leisure-augmented measure on the OWN-WEIGHTS bundle under

\caption{The closure matrix with the three welfare measures. $W_a$ is
the T\"ornqvist index of household consumption (the measure currently
reported); $W_a'$ the exact money-metric of consumption, on the same base;
$W_b$ the CES quantity aggregate over $c+g$ at $\lambda=1$, $\sigma=0.9$ ---
which is \emph{not} the value ratio, and differs from it at first order
wherever the basket does not grow proportionally, as the programme cells
do; $B^{\mathrm{own}}$ the own-weights bundle aggregate --- each state's
$c+g$ valued by its own composition weights, which reduces identically to
$\sum_i f_i$, the bundle value ratio at base prices; it is the
preference-consistent bundle measure and carries the F1 rows, where the
fixed-weight aggregates are not defined (see the dagger);
$W_c$ that same own-weights bundle less the value of the
additional work $w\,\Delta N$, to first order, under the two saving
conventions; it therefore inherits the bundle column's regime-consistency,
to first order, under the two saving conventions. $W_a$ and $W_a'$ coincide
except under F1, whose preference shifter moves the basket off proportional
growth. Macro columns: the recorded manifest fields, all in percent against
the reference continuation. \textsuperscript{\ddag}~F1 rows report the
consumption measures, $B^{\mathrm{own}}$ and $W_c$, but not the fixed-weight
aggregates. Under F1 the preference weights are themselves shifted, so the
fixed-weight CES has no utility foundation: on the same consumption basket it
sits about $0.47$ pp below the exact money-metric in every F1 cell, and
would report the intended reallocation as a loss; the own-weights aggregate,
being regime-consistent, is unaffected. \texttt{experiments/welfare-f1-decomp.jl}
and \texttt{experiments/welfare-ownweights.jl} reproduce the two.
}
